title: An affine conormal basis gives a sheaf frame and its stalk rank
statement: Let $i:Z\to Y$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], $U\subseteq Y$ an affine open [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $A=\Gamma(Y,U)$, $I=\ker(i^\sharp_U)$ the ideal $i.\mathrm{ker}.\mathrm{ideal}(U)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and $V=i^{-1}(U)$. Let $m\in\mathbf N$ and let $b$ be an $A/I$-module basis of $I/I^2$ indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}(m)$, where $I/I^2$ denotes the quotient of the module $I$ by the submodule generated by products of two elements of $I$. Set $C=i^*\mathcal I$ for the tensor pullback of the kernel ideal sheaf [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $C$ on the over-$V$ site is isomorphic to the free structure module indexed by $\mathrm{ULift}(\mathrm{Fin}(m))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Moreover, for every $z\in Z$ with $i(z)\in U$, the module stalk $C_z$ [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] has finrank $m$ over $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$. No regularity or Noetherian hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text: The affine closed-immersion criterion makes V affine and i.app U surjective. Hom.ker_apply identifies I with the kernel of this ring map. RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective, preceded by Ideal.quotEquivOfEq, gives q:A/I ≃ O_Z(V) with q(a mod I)=i.app U(a). Apply affine_conormal_sections with the identity coordinate ring equivalence to obtain quasi-coherence of C and an A-linear equivalence e:I/I^2 ≃ C(V).

Define the additive coordinate isomorphism (Fin m →_0 O_Z(V)) → C(V) by first applying q^{-1} to every coefficient, then b.repr^{-1}, then e. For a scalar c∈O_Z(V), choose a lift a∈A by surjectivity. The formula q^{-1}(i.app U(a))=a mod I shows that coefficientwise scalar multiplication becomes multiplication by a mod I. Linearity of b.repr^{-1} and A-linearity of e turn the result into i.app U(a) times the image. Thus this additive isomorphism is O_Z(V)-linear. Reindex along the ULift equivalence.

Restrict C along the affine chart fromSpec:Spec O_Z(V)→Z. The proved source-library sectionsRestrictFromSpecLinearEquiv identifies its global section module with C(V). Compose with the inverse coordinate isomorphism from the previous step. Since the restriction is quasi-coherent, Mathlib isIso_fromTildeΓ_of_isQuasicoherent identifies it with the sheaf of its global sections. Apply tilde.functor.mapIso to the coordinate module isomorphism and compose with tildeFinsupp. Restrict this free frame back along V.isoSpec.hom, and use restrictCompIso, restrictFreeIso and overIsoFreeEquiv to obtain the displayed over-V frame.

For any z∈V, use the coordinate projections and inclusions of this over-V frame. On a neighbourhood W of z, take their values on W∩V and then germs. These compatible maps give an additive coordinate cocone on the neighbourhood diagram and hence maps out of the stalk; compatibility with germ scalar multiplication makes each coordinate map O_{Z,z}-linear. The germs of the basis inclusions on V give m vectors. Projection-inclusion identities give Kronecker-delta coordinates. The finite sum of inclusion-projection composites is the identity of C|_V, so, after representing any stalk element by a section on a neighbourhood contained in V, its germ equals the sum of its coordinates times the basis germs. These two identities prove the coordinate map C_z→(ULift(Fin m)→O_{Z,z}) bijective. Use LinearEquiv.finrank_eq and the standard finite-product finrank formula over the nontrivial scheme stalk ring to obtain m. All maps are actual cocone constructions, with no postponed proof. Empty m gives empty sums, and empty V makes the pointwise assertion vacuous.

theorem affine_conormal_frame {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (U : Y.affineOpens) (m : ℕ)
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin m) (Γ(Y, U.1) ⧸ i.ker.ideal U) (i.ker.ideal U).Cotangent) :
    Nonempty ((((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj i.ker.toModules).over
        (i ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)) ≅ SheafOfModules.free (ULift.{u} (Fin m))) ∧
      ∀ z : Z, i z ∈ U.1 →
        Module.finrank (Z.presheaf.stalk z)
          ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Z.toRingedSpace z).obj
            ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj i.ker.toModules)) = m
